blocks.text:
Breakfast at the hotel. Transfer to the airport for your flight home.

Over 10 days, the route takes you through several very different landscapes: the neighbourhoods of Buenos Aires, the glaciers of El Calafate, the steppes and fjords of Chile, the granite towers of Torres del Paine, the Strait of Magellan and Santiago at the foot of the Andes.

Patagonia makes a strong impression through its sheer scale. After several days among glaciers, steppes, rock and water, familiar distances begin to feel different. There is little dense development here, and long stretches of the route pass through almost empty terrain.

Another feature of the route is the combination of exploring on land and travelling by boat. In Torres del Paine, you travel along the national park's roads and trails; at Perito Moreno, you view the glacier from observation platforms; and in the Strait of Magellan, you take to the water by boat. This lets you experience Patagonia through different ways of travelling around the region as well as through different countries.
